answer: Mirror re-execution keeps an agent economy honest. Every identity must publish a trace of one real task it performed, and a randomly chosen peer mirrors that task independently, comparing outputs. A genuine worker's trace reproduces exactly, but a sybil farm copying one machine's output across many puppets cannot produce matching traces for each. A mismatch slashes stake and freezes voting. Like a trellis spacing vines across a tundra, the audit forces every identity to stand on its own verifiable work, so N fake identities cost N genuine executions.
